evidence:
Source-based weight review only. The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks row 45 requires real functionality to outweigh structure/style; Internal row 45 explicitly describes the 60% functional allocation and internal verifier weights. Frozen task/tests/scoring.toml:5-11 uses functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2 and functional floor=0.05. Policy and score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (SHA256 95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba and 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e). score.py:40-48 gives the gates no mass, applies a strict functional>0.05 floor, and calculates the weighted mean. Parsing all scored criteria gives 80 functional rows totaling 45.25, six Polish rows totaling 3, and six Visual rows totaling 6.

Relative importance is credible: functional/judge.toml:135-147 weights supported-loop deadline/rollback 2.50/0.75; :331-357 weights process durability 1.80 and stale-save refusal/draft retention 1.80/1.40; :499-581 allocates 13.80 (30.50% of functional; 18.30% of overall reward) to twelve history, restore, retry, race and restart outcomes. These match the defining preserve-working-preview and saved-version promises in instruction.md:3 and behaviour.md:29-40. By contrast, editor monospace/line numbers/colouring at functional/judge.toml:296-315 total only 0.50 (0.663 percentage points overall), and duration display at :254-259/:401-406 totals 0.20. Thus behavioral function carries 59.337% overall even if all three editor presentation rows are counted as nonfunctional; the combined remaining mass is 40.663%. Polish gives mobile operability and understandable workspace organization 1.0 each, with four separate accessibility outcomes 0.25 each (polish/judge.toml:17-68). Visual has six equally weighted anchored craft outcomes; it cannot contribute more than 20%.

Adversarial reasoning: a beautiful static editor fails render/judge.toml:25; a localStorage-only library fails constraints/judge.toml:25-27. Merely granting the three editor presentation rows gives functional=0.50/45.25=0.01105, below the floor, so style alone cannot collect reward. The canonical low floor does allow an incomplete but genuinely executing/shared-saving app into shaping: an illustrative 3.55/45.25 functional score vector plus even perfect Polish/Visual produces 0.4471, not a high score. This arithmetic is not an executed weak app or a bound on every partial implementation. A conforming app with a simple/native palette, alternative pane layout and native focus remains eligible for full presentation credit under polish/judge.toml:23,50,68 and visual/judge.toml:40,55,70,85; no weight requires bespoke decoration. No concrete weight distortion was found.

All 21 hashes in raw-evidence-index.json match their current artifacts. Its stated limits explicitly deny a configured-judge/model score; none is claimed here. This row passes the source/arithmetic check only and does not clear the separate required runtime, reward-discrimination or ordering evidence gaps.
